title: Vows & Contemplations
subtitle: Yoga-sūtra of Patañjali with the Yoga-bhāṣya attributed to Vyāsa
source: English: James Haughton Woods, The Yoga-System of Patañjali (Harvard Oriental Series 17, 1914; public domain). Sanskrit sūtras: sanskritdocuments.org. Vyāsa-bhāṣya (IAST): GRETIL, Ānandāśrama Sanskrit Series 47. Vācaspati's sub-commentary is not included.

entries.title: The five yamas
entries.transliteration: ahiṃsāsatyāsteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ
entries.translation: Abstinence from injury and from falsehood and from theft and from incontinence and from acceptance of gifts are the abstentions.
entries.commentary_en:
Of these [five] abstinence from injury means the abstinence from malice towards all living creatures in every way and at all times. And the other abstentions and observances are rooted in it. In so far as their aim is the perfection of it, they are taught in order to teach it.

And in this sense it has been said, "Surely this same brahman in proportion as he desires to take upon himself many courses-of-action, in this proportion refraining from heedlessly giving injury, fulfils [the abstention of] abstinence from injury in order to give it the full character of its spotlessness." Abstinence-from-falsehood (satya) means speech and mind such as correspond to the object-intended; and speech and mind corresponding to what is seen or inferred or heard.

If speech is spoken in order that one's own knowledge may pass to some one else, it should not be deceitful or mistaken or barren of information; [then it would be abstinence from falsehood]. It should be used for the service of all; not for the ruin of creatures.

And even when used thus, should it be only for the ruin of creatures, it would not be an abstinence from falsehood; it would be nothing less than wrong. In so far as there would be a false kind of merit [and] a resemblance of merit, it would become the worst of evils.

Therefore let [the yogin] consider [first] what is good for all creatures and [then] speak with abstinence-from-falsehood. Theft is the unauthorized (apāstrapūrvaka) appropriation of things-of-value from another. While abstinence-from-theft, when free from coveting, is the refusal to do this. Continence is control of the hidden organ of generation.

Abstinence-from-acceptance-of-gifts is abstinence-from-appropriating objects, because one sees the disadvantages in acquiring them or keeping them or losing them or in being attached to them or in harming them. These then are the abstentions.
entries.commentary_sa:
tatrāhiṃsā sarvathā sarvadā sarvabhūtānām anabhidrohaḥ. uttare ca yamaniyamās tanmūlās tatsiddhiparatayaiva tatpratipādanāya pratipādyante. tadavadātarūpakaraṇāyaivopādīyante. tathā coktam --- sa khalv ayaṃ brāhmaṇo yathā yathā vratāni bahūni samāditsate tathā tathā pramādakṛtebhyo hiṃsānidānebhyo nivartamānas tām evāvadātarūpām ahiṃsāṃ karoti. satyaṃ yathārthe vāṅmanase.

yathā dṛṣṭaṃ yathānumitaṃ tathā vāṅ manaś ceti. paratra svabodhasaṃkrāntaye vāg uktā, sā yadi na vañcitā bhrāntā vā pratipattivandhyā vā bhaved iti. eṣā sarvabhūtopakārārthaṃ pravṛttā na bhūtopaghātāya. yadi caivam apy abhidhīyamānā bhūtopaghātaparaiva syān na satyaṃ bhavet pāpam eva bhavet tena puṇyābhāsena puṇyapratirūpakeṇa kaṣṭaṃ tamaḥ prāpnuyāt.

tasmāt parīkṣya sarvabhūtahitaṃ satyaṃ brūyāt. steyam aśāstrapūrvakaṃ dravyāṇāṃ parataḥ svīkaraṇaṃ, tatpratiṣedhaḥ punar aspṛhārūpam asteyam iti. brahmacaryaṃ guptendriyasyopasthasya saṃyamaḥ. viṣayāṇām arjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṅgahiṃsādoṣadarśanād asvīkaraṇam aparigraha ity ete yamāḥ.

entries.title: The Great Vow (mahāvrata)
entries.transliteration: jātideśakālasamayānavacchinnāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratam
entries.translation: When they are unqualified by species or place or time or exigency and when [covering] all [these] classes — [under these circumstances exists] the Great Course-of-conduct.
entries.commentary_en:
Of these [five], abstinence-from-injury is qualified in respect of species as follows, a catcher of fish does injury to fishes only and to nothing else. — The same is qualified in respect of place, as when one says, 'I will not slay in a holy place.' — The same is qualified in respect of time, as when one says, 'I will not slay on the fourteenth day [of the lunar fortnight] nor on a day of good omen.' — The same, in the case of one who refrains from [these] three is qualified in respect of exigency, as when one says, 'For the sake of gods and brahmans and not otherwise I will slay.' Likewise also in the case of the warrior who says, 'In battle only [I will do] injury, and nowhere else.' Abstinence-from-injury and the other [abstinences] unqualified by these species or times or places or exigencies must be kept when [covering] no less than all [these] cases.

'In all [these] classes' means with regard to all [these] objects. Without exceptions in no less than all [these] classes — this is what is meant by speaking of the Great Course-of-conduct when [covering] all [these] stages.
entries.commentary_sa:
tatrāhiṃsā jātyavacchinnā matsyavadhakasya matsyeṣv eva nānyatra hiṃsā. saiva deśāvacchinnā na tīrthe haniṣyāmīti. saiva kālāvacchinnā na caturdaśyāṃ na puṇye 'hani haniṣyāmīti. saiva tribhir uparatasya samayāvacchinnā devabrāhmaṇārthe nānyathā haniṣyāmīti. yathā ca kṣatriyāṇāṃ yuddha eva hiṃsā nānyatreti.

ebhir jātideśakālasamayair anavacchinnā ahiṃsādayaḥ sarvathaiva paripālanīyāḥ. sarvabhūmiṣu sarvaviṣayeṣu sarvathaivāviditavyabhicārāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratam ity ucyante.

entries.title: The five niyamas
entries.transliteration: śaucasaṃtoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ
entries.translation: Cleanliness and contentment and self-castigation and study and devotion to the Īśvara are the observances.
entries.commentary_en:
Of these [five], cleanliness is produced by earth or by water or the like, and by the consumption and other [requirements] with regard to pure sacrificial food. This is outer.

Inner [cleanliness] is the washing away of the blemishes of the mind-stuff. — [To practise] contentment means not to covet more than the means at hand. — Self-castigation is the bearing of extremes, hunger and thirst, cold and heat, standing and sitting, stock-stillness and formal stillness, and, according to usage, courses-of-conduct such as mortifications (kṛcchra) and lunar fasts and rigid penances. — Study is the recital of books that treat of release or the repetition of the syllable of adoration (praṇava). — Devotion to the Īśvara is the offering up of all actions to the Supreme Teacher.

"He who rests in himself, for whom the network of perverse-considerations (vitarka) has been destroyed, whether resting upon a bed or on a seat, or wandering upon a road, would behold the destruction of the seed of the round-of-rebirths, would be permanently released, would participate in deathless delights." With regard to which this has been said, [i. 29], "Thereafter comes the right knowledge of him who thinks in an inverse way, and the removal of obstacles."
entries.commentary_sa:
tatra śaucaṃ mṛjjalādijanitaṃ medhyābhyavaharaṇādi ca bāhyam. ābhyantaraṃ cittamalānām ākṣālanam. saṃtoṣaḥ saṃnihitasādhanād adhikasyānupāditsā. tapo dvaṃdvasahanam. dvaṃdvāś ca jighatsāpipāse śītoṣṇe sthānāsane kāṣṭhamaunākāramaune ca. vratāni caiṣāṃ yathāyogaṃ kṛcchracāndrāyaṇasāṃtapanādīni. svādhyāyo mokṣaśāstrāṇām adhyayanaṃ praṇavajapo vā.

īśvarapraṇidhānaṃ tasmin paramagurau sarvakarmārpaṇam. śayyāsanastho 'tha pathi vrajan vā svasthaḥ parikṣīṇavitarkajālaḥ / saṃsārabījakṣayam īkṣamāṇaḥ syān nityayukto 'mṛtabhogabhāgī // yatredam uktaṃ tataḥ pratyakcetanādhigamo 'py antarāyābhāvaś ceti.

entries.title: When contrary thoughts arise
entries.transliteration: vitarkabādhane pratipakṣabhāvanam
entries.translation: If there be inhibition by perverse-considerations (vitarka), there should be cultivation of the opposites.
entries.intro_en: As for these abstentions and observances,
entries.commentary_en:
Whenever [in the mind] of this brahman [practising the abstentions and observances] injuries and similar [faults] arise as perverse-considerations, such as for instance, 'I will kill him who hurts me; I will also lie; I will also appropriate his money; and I will commit adultery with his wife; and I will also make myself master of his property.' Thus inhibited by the blazing fever of perverse-considerations, let him cultivate the opposites of these.

Let him ponder, 'Baked upon the pitiless coals of the round-of-rebirths, I take my refuge in the rules (dharma) for yoga by giving protection to every living creature. I myself after ridding myself of perverse-considerations am betaking myself to them once more, like a dog.

As a dog to his vomit, even so I betake myself to that of which I had rid myself.' Other similar [inhibitions of perverse-considerations] should be applied in the other sutras also [upon the aids to yoga].
entries.commentary_sa:
yadāsya brāhmaṇasya hiṃsādayo vitarkā jāyeran haniṣyāmy aham apakāriṇam anṛtam api vakṣyāmi dravyam apy asya svīkariṣyāmi dāreṣu cāsya vyavāyī bhaviṣyāmi parigraheṣu cāsya svāmī bhaviṣyāmīti. evam unmārgapravaṇavitarkajvareṇātidīptena bādhyamānas tatpratipakṣān bhāvayet. ghoreṣu saṃsārāṅgāreṣu pacyamānena mayā śaraṇam upāgataḥ sarvabhūtābhayapradānena yogadharmaḥ.

sa khalv ahaṃ tyaktvā vitarkān punas tān ādadānas tulyaḥ śvavṛtteneti bhāvayet. yathā śvā vāntāvalehī tathā tyaktasya punar ādadāna iti. evamādi sūtrāntareṣv api yojyam.

entries.title: Contrary thoughts and their consequences
entries.transliteration: vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam
entries.translation: Since perverse-considerations such as injuries, whether done or caused to be done or approved, whether ensuing upon greed or anger or infatuation, whether mild or moderate or vehement, find their unending consequences in pain and in lack of thinking, there should be the cultivation of their opposites.
entries.commentary_en:
Of these [considerations], first of all, injury, since it is done or caused to be done or approved, is three-fold.

Moreover, each of these is three-fold, in so far as there is greed [such as] desire for the meat or for the skin, or in so far as there is anger as when a man thinks he has been 'hurt by that man', or in so far as there is infatuation as when a man thinks [that what he is doing] 'will be merit for me'.

Again, since greed and anger and infatuation are three-fold as being mild and moderate and vehement, there are thus seven-and-twenty varieties of injuries.

Yet again, since [these are] gentle and moderate and extreme [these are] three-fold as follows, gently mild and moderately mild and keenly mild; similarly, gently moderate and moderately moderate and keenly moderate; likewise, gently keen and moderately keen and vehemently keen. Thus injury is of one-and-eighty varieties.

It is, however, innumerable because of the varieties due to specifications (niyama) and to options (vikalpa) and to aggregations (samuccaya), due to the fact that the varieties of those-who-breathe-the-breath-of-life are innumerable. In the same manner [the classification] is to be applied to falsehood and to the other [crimes].

Now since these perverse considerations have endless consequences in pain and in lack of thinking, one should cultivate their opposites.

[In other words], there is a cultivation of those things the endless consequences of which are pain and a lack of thinking. — And to continue, he who commits an injury first of all reduces the strength of the victim, then causes him pain by falling upon him with a knife or something of the kind, [and] afterwards even deprives him of life.

When once he has taken away [the victim's] strength, his own animate or inanimate aids begin to have their strength dwindle away. As a result of causing pain, he himself experiences pain in hells and in [the bodies of] animals and of departed spirits and in other [forms].

As a result of uprooting [the victim] from life, he himself continues from moment to moment at the very point of departure from life. And even while wishing for death he pants laboriously since the fruition of pain is to be felt in a fruition which has a limit [in time].

Furthermore, even if [the effects of] injury could be somehow done away by merit, even then, if he obtained happiness, it would be [on condition that] his length-of-life be short. — In the same way, so far as possible, [the classification] is to be applied to lying and to the other [violations of the abstentions].

Thus pondering on that same [painful consequence] of perverse considerations, which is inevitable (anugata) and undesired, the yogin should not devote his central organ to perverse considerations. As a result of the cultivation of the opposites, the perverse considerations become things that may be escaped.
entries.commentary_sa:
tatra hiṃsā tāvat --- kṛtā kāritānumoditeti tridhā. ekaikā punas tridhā lobhena māṃsacarmārthena krodhenāpakṛtam aneneti mohena dharmo me bhaviṣyatīti. lobhakrodhamohāḥ punas trividhā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā iti. evaṃ saptaviṃśatir bhedā bhavanti hiṃsāyāḥ. mṛdumadhyādhimātrāḥ punas tridhā --- mṛdumṛdur madhyamṛdus tīvramṛdur iti. tathā mṛdumadhyo madhyamadhyas tīvramadhya iti.

tathā mṛdutīvro madhyatīvro 'dhimātratīvra iti. evam ekāśītibhedā hiṃsā bhavati. sā punar niyamavikalpasamuccayabhedād asaṃkhyeyā, prāṇabhṛdbhedasyāparisaṃkhyeyatvād iti. evam anṛtādiṣv api yojyam. te khalv amī vitarkā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam. duḥkham ajñānaṃ cānantaṃ phalaṃ yeṣām iti pratipakṣabhāvanam.

tathā ca hiṃsakas tāvat prathamaṃ vadhyasya vīryam ākṣipati. tataś ca śastrādinipātena duḥkhayati. tato jīvitād api mocayati. tato vīryākṣepād asya cetanācetanam upakaraṇaṃ kṣīṇavīryaṃ bhavati.

duḥkhotpādān narakatiryakpretādiṣu duḥkham anubhavati, jīvitavyaparopaṇāt pratikṣaṇaṃ ca jīvitātyaye vartamāno maraṇam icchann api duḥkhavipākasya niyatavipākavedanīyatvāt kathaṃcid evocchvasiti. yadi ca kathaṃcit puṇyāvāpagatā hiṃsā bhavet tatra sukhaprāptau bhaved alpāyur iti. evam anṛtādiṣv api yojyaṃ yathāsaṃbhavam.

evaṃ vitarkāṇāṃ cāmum evānugataṃ vipākam aniṣṭaṃ bhāvayan na vitarkeṣu manaḥ praṇidadhīta.

entries.title: Ahiṃsā — result
entries.transliteration: ahiṃsāpratiṣṭhāyāṃ tatsaṃnidhau vairatyāgaḥ
entries.translation: As soon as he is grounded in abstinence from injury, his presence begets a suspension of enmity.
entries.intro_en: When [the perverse considerations] become for this [yogin] unsuitable for generation, then the power caused by this fact becomes indicative of the yogin's perfection. For example,
entries.commentary_en: [This] occurs on the part of all living creatures.

entries.title: Satya — result
entries.transliteration: satyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ kriyāphalāśrayatvam
entries.translation: As soon as he is grounded in abstinence from falsehood, actions and consequences depend upon him.
entries.commentary_en: If [the yogin] says to a man (iti), 'Be thou right-living,' the man becomes right-living. If he expresses the wish (iti) 'Attain thou heaven,' the man attains heaven. What he says (vāk) comes true.
entries.commentary_sa: dhārmiko bhūyā iti bhavati dhārmikaḥ, svargaṃ prāpnuhīti svargaṃ prāpnoti amoghāsya vāg bhavati.

entries.title: Asteya — result
entries.transliteration: asteyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ sarvaratnopasthānam
entries.translation: As soon as he is grounded in abstinence from theft, all jewels approach him.
entries.commentary_en: From all directions jewels approach to be his.

entries.title: Brahmacarya — result
entries.transliteration: brahmacaryapratiṣṭhāyāṃ vīryalābhaḥ
entries.translation: As soon as he is grounded in abstinence from incontinence, he acquires energy.
entries.commentary_en: By the acquisition of which the yogin increases [his] unhindered qualities. And when he is perfected he is able to transfer [his] thinking to [his] pupils.
entries.commentary_sa: yasya lābhād apratighān guṇān utkarṣayati. siddhaś ca vineyeṣu jñānam ādhātuṃ samartho bhavatīti.

entries.title: Aparigraha — result
entries.transliteration: aparigrahasthairye janmakathaṃtāsaṃbodhaḥ
entries.translation: As soon as he is established in abstinence-from-acceptance-of-gifts, a thorough illumination upon the conditions of birth —
entries.commentary_en: — Becomes his. 'Who was I? How was I? Or what [can] this birth be? Or how [can] this [birth] be? Or what shall we become? Or how shall we become?' Such a desire to know his own condition in former and later and intermediate times becomes of itself fulfilled for him. These when he is established in the abstentions are the perfections.
entries.commentary_sa: asya bhavati ko 'ham āsaṃ katham aham āsaṃ kiṃsvid idaṃ kathaṃsvid idaṃ ke vā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kathaṃ vā bhaviṣyāma ity evam asya pūrvāntaparāntamadhyeṣv ātmabhāvajijāsā svarūpeṇopāvartate. etā yamasthairye siddhayaḥ.

entries.title: Śauca — result
entries.transliteration: śaucāt svāṅgajugupsā parair asaṃsargaḥ
entries.translation: As a result of cleanliness there is disgust at one's own body and no intercourse with others.
entries.intro_en: We will speak with regard to observances.
entries.commentary_en:
As soon as there is disgust with his own body, he has begun cleanliness. Seeing the offensiveness of the body, he is no longer attached to the body and becomes an ascetic (yati). Moreover there is no intercourse with others.

Perceiving the true nature of the body, desirous of escaping even his own body, even after he has washed it with earth and water and other [substances], not seeing any purity in the body, how could he have intercourse with the bodies of others absolutely unhallowed as they are?
entries.commentary_sa: svāṅge jugupsāyāṃ śaucam ārabhamāṇaḥ kāyāvadyadarśī kāyānabhiṣvaṅgī yatir bhavati. kiṃca parair asaṃsargaḥ kāyasvabhāvāvalokī svam api kāyaṃ jihāsur mṛjjalādibhir ākṣālayann api kāyaśuddhim apaśyan kathaṃ parakāyair atyantam evāprayataiḥ saṃsṛjyeta.

entries.title: Śauca — further results
entries.transliteration: sattvaśuddhisaumanasyaikāgryendriyajayātmadarśanayogyatvāni ca
entries.translation: Purity of sattva and gentleness and singleness-of-intent and subjugation of the senses and fitness for the sight of the self —
entries.commentary_en:
The word 'arise' completes the sentence. As a result of cleanliness there is purity of sattva; therefrom [it acquires] gentleness; from this [it acquires] singleness-of-intent; therefrom [it acquires] subjugation of the senses; and from this fitness for the sight of the self is acquired by the sattva of the thinking-substance.

So to this [last] there is access, as a result of his being established in cleanliness.
entries.commentary_sa: bhavantīti vākyaśeṣaḥ. śuceḥ sattvaśuddhis tataḥ saumanasyaṃ tata aikāgryaṃ tata indriyajayas tataś cātmadarśanayogyatvaṃ buddhisattvasya bhavatīty etac chaucasthairyād adhigamyata iti.

entries.title: Saṃtoṣa — result
entries.transliteration: saṃtoṣād anuttamaḥ sukhalābhaḥ
entries.translation: As a result of contentment there is an acquisition of superlative pleasure.
entries.commentary_en: And in this sense it has been said, "What constitutes the pleasure of love in this world and what the supreme pleasure of heaven are both not to be compared with the sixteenth part of the pleasure of dwindled craving (tṛṣṇā)."
entries.commentary_sa: tathā coktam --- "yac ca kāmasukhaṃ loke yac ca divyaṃ mahat sukham / tṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaite nārhataḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ kalām" iti.

entries.title: Tapas — result
entries.transliteration: kāyendriyasiddhir aśuddhikṣayāt tapasaḥ
entries.translation: Perfection in the body and in the organs after impurity has dwindled as a result of self-castigation.
entries.commentary_en: Self-castigation in the very act of completing itself destroys the defilement from the covering of impurity. As a result of the removal of the defilement of the covering of this [impurity] there is perfection of the body, such as atomization [iii. 45]; likewise perfection of the organs, such as hearing and seeing at a distance [that is, telepathy].
entries.commentary_sa: nirvartyamānam eva tapo hinasty aśuddhyāvaraṇamalaṃ tadāvaraṇamalāpagamāt kāyasiddhir aṇimādyā. tathendriyasiddhir dūrāc chravaṇadarśanādyeti.

entries.title: Svādhyāya — result
entries.transliteration: svādhyāyād iṣṭadevatāsaṃprayogaḥ
entries.translation: As a result of study there is communion with the chosen deity.
entries.commentary_en: Gods and sages and perfected men come within the range of vision of [the yogin] who has the disposition to study; and are helpful to his work.
entries.commentary_sa: devā ṛṣayaḥ siddhāś ca svādhyāyaśīlasya darśanaṃ gacchanti, kārye cāsya vartanta iti.

entries.title: Īśvarapraṇidhāna — result
entries.transliteration: samādhisiddhir īśvarapraṇidhānāt
entries.translation: Perfection of concentration as a result of devotion to the Īśvara.
entries.commentary_en: One whose whole nature is surrendered to the Īśvara has perfection of concentration. By which [concentration] he knows as the thing really is (avitatham) all that he desires to know, in other places and in other bodies and in other times. Thereafter his insight sees into things as they are (yathābhūtam).
entries.commentary_sa: īśvarārpitasarvabhāvasya samādhisiddhir yayā sarvam īpsitam avitathaṃ jānāti deśāntare dehāntare kālāntare ca. tato 'sya prajñā yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti.

entries.title: Maitrī · Karuṇā · Muditā · Upekṣā
entries.transliteration: maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣāṇāṃ sukhaduḥkhapuṇyāpuṇyaviṣayāṇāṃ bhāvanātaś cittaprasādanam
entries.translation: By the cultivation of friendliness towards happiness and compassion towards pain and joy towards merit and indifference towards demerit [the yogin should attain] the undisturbed calm of the mind-stuff.
entries.intro_en: Of which [stable mind-stuff] this purification is enjoined by the system. By what means is this?
entries.commentary_en:
Of these [four] he should cultivate friendliness towards all living beings that have reached the experience of happiness; compassion towards those in pain; joy towards those whose character is meritorious; indifference towards those whose character is demeritorious. When he thus cultivates [friendliness and the rest] the white quality [of karma] comes into being [within him].

And then the mind-stuff becomes calm; and when calm it becomes single-in-intent and reaches the stable state.
entries.commentary_sa: tatra sarvaprāṇiṣu sukhasaṃbhogāpanneṣu maitrīṃ bhāvayet. duḥkhiteṣu karuṇām. puṇyātmakeṣu muditām. apuṇyaśīleṣūpekṣām. evam asya bhāvayataḥ śuklo dharma upajāyate. tataś ca cittaṃ prasīdati. prasannam ekāgraṃ sthitipadaṃ labhate.

groups.name: Devī Atharvaśīrṣa
groups.subtitleEn: Teachings by Ācārya Sthaneshwar Timalsina, Śrī Devī Atharvaśīrṣa (Vimarsha Publications). English from the book.

entries.title: The Deities Approach Devī
entries.transliteration: oṃ sarve vai devā devīm-upatasthuḥ kāsi tvaṃ mahādevīti || 1 ||
entries.translation: Oṃ. All (sarva) the deities (deva) indeed (vai) approached in worship (upatasthuḥ) toward the Goddess (devī): “Who (kā) are (asi) you (tvam), O Great Goddess (mahādevī)?” [they asked] thus (iti).

entries.title: Ātmastuti: Devī Replies
entries.transliteration: sā abravīd-ahaṃ brahma-svarūpiṇī | mattaḥ prakṛti-puruṣātmakaṃ jagat | śūnyaṃ cāśūnyaṃ ca || 2 ||
entries.translation: She (sā) replied (abravīt): “I am (aham) the very form (svarūpiṇī) of Brahman. From me (mattaḥ), [emerged] this entire cosmos (jagat), comprising (ātmaka) material nature (prakṛti) and pure consciousness (puruṣa), which is both (ca) empty (śūnya) and (ca) not empty (aśūnya) .” Ātmastuti: Devī’s Reply Begins

entries.title: Ātmastuti: Devī Subsumes All Dichotomies I
entries.transliteration: aham-ānandānānandau | ahaṃ vijñānāvijñāne | ahaṃ brahmābrahmaṇī veditavye | ahaṃ pañca-bhūtāny-apañca-bhūtāni | aham-akhilaṃ jagat || 3 ||
entries.translation: “I am (aham) bliss (ānanda) and misery (anānanda). I am (aham) knowledge (vijñāna) and ignorance (avijñāna). I am (aham) to be known (veditavya) as the transcendent reality (brahman) and the immanent reality (abrahman). I am (aham) the five elements (pañcabhūta) and what is beyond the five elements (apañcabhūta). I am (aham) the totality (akhila) of all that exists (jagat) .”

entries.title: Ātmastuti: Devī Subsumes All Dichotomies II
entries.transliteration: vedo ’ham avedo ’ham | vidyā ’ham avidyā ’ham | ajā ’ham anajā ’ham | adhaś cordhvaṃ ca tiryak cāham || 4 ||
entries.translation: “I am (aham) the absolute knowledge (veda) and I am (aham) the phenomenal knowledge (aveda). I am (aham) knowledge (vidyā) and I am (aham) ignorance (avidyā). I am (aham) the unborn (ajā) and I am (aham) that which is born (anajā). I am (aham) below (adhas), above (ūrdhvam), and (ca) across (tiryak) .”

entries.title: Ātmastuti: Vāk Sūkta I
entries.transliteration: ahaṃ rudrebhir vasubhiś carāmi | ahamādityair uta viśvadevaiḥ | ahaṃ mitrāvaruṇāvubhau bibharmi | aham-indrāgnī aham-aśvināvubhau || 5 ||
entries.translation: I (aham) move about (carāmi) through the Rudras [deities of the intermediate realm] and the Vasus [deities of the terrestrial realm]. I (aham) am with the Ādityas [deities of the heavenly realm] and (uta) the Viśvadevas [grouping of deities]. I (aham) sustain (bibharmi) both (ubha) Mitra and Varuṇa. I (aham) [sustain] Indra [king of deities] and Agni [the fire deity]. I (aham) [sustain] both (ubha) the Aśvins [twin deities].

entries.title: Ātmastuti: Vāk Sūkta II
entries.transliteration: ahaṃ somaṃ tvaṣṭāraṃ pūṣaṇaṃ bhagaṃ dadhāmi | ahaṃ viṣṇum-uru-kramaṃ brahmāṇamuta prajāpatiṃ dadhāmi || 6 ||
entries.translation: I (aham) hold within me (dadhāmi) Soma [the lunar deity], [and the solar deities like] Tvaṣṭṛ [the divine artisan], Pūṣan [the divine guide], and Bhaga [the giver of wealth]. I (aham) hold within me (dadhāmi) Viṣṇu who takes wide strides (urukrama) [in his Vāmana form, as one of the Ādityas], [and the deities associated with creation:] Brahmā, and (uta) Prajāpati.

entries.title: Ātmastuti: Vāk Sūkta III
entries.transliteration: ahaṃ dadhāmi draviṇaṃ haviṣmate suprāvye yajamānāya sunvate | ahaṃ rāṣṭrī saṅgamanī vasūnāṃ cikituṣī prathamā yajñiyānām | ahaṃ suve pitaram-asya mūrdhan-mama yonirapsvantaḥ samudre | ya evaṃ veda | sa daivīṃ sampadam-āpnoti || 7 ||
entries.translation: I (aham) bestow (dadhāmi) prosperity (draviṇa) upon the one who makes the ritual offerings (haviṣmat), the one who sponsors the ritual (yajamāna), the one who is worthy of protection (suprāvye), and the one who presses out (sunvat) [the soma during the ritual]. I (aham) am the sovereign (rāṣṭrī) who brings together (saṅgamanī) all the Vasus [deities of the terrestrial realm], the one who knows (cikituṣī) [all], foremost (prathama) among those to be worshiped (yajñiya). I (aham) give birth to (suve) the father (pitṛ) of all this (asya), [placing him] at the head (mūrdhan) [of the cosmos]; my (mama) womb (yoni) is in the water (ap) [below] within (antar) the [primordial] ocean (samudra) [of creation, from which all emerges]. Whoever (yaḥ) knows (veda) thus (evam) attains (āpnoti) the divine qualities (daivī sampad).

entries.title: The Deities Revere Devī: Aparājitā Stotra
entries.transliteration: te devā abruvan – namo devyai mahādevyai śivāyai satataṃ namaḥ | namaḥ prakṛtyai bhadrāyai niyatāḥ praṇatāḥ sma tām || 8 ||
entries.translation: The (te) deities (deva) replied (abruvan): “Reverence (namas) to the Goddess (devī), the Great Goddess (mahādevī). Constant (satatam) reverence (namas) to her, the auspicious one (śivā). Reverence (namas) to she who is nature (prakṛti) and the granter of good fortune (bhadrā). Indeed (sma), we bow down (praṇata) and remain disciplined (niyata) to her (tām) .” Taking Shelter in Devī as Durgā

entries.title: Taking Shelter in Devī: Durgā Sūkta
entries.transliteration: tām agni-varṇāṃ tapasā jvalantīṃ vairocanīṃ karma-phaleṣu juṣṭām | durgāṃ devīṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadyāmahe ’surān nāśayitryai te namaḥ || 9 ||
entries.translation: Unto her (tad), who has the hue (varṇa) of fire (agni), blazing (jvalantī) with heat (tapas), radiant like the sun (vairocanī), Goddess Durgā (durgā devī), who is gratified (juṣṭa) by the fruits of our actions (karmaphala): in your shelter (śaraṇa), we arrive (prapadyāmahe). Reverence (namas) to you (te), the destroyer (nāśayitrī) of asuras.

entries.title: Calling Forth Devī as Vāc
entries.transliteration: devīṃ vācam-ajanayanta devās tāṃ viśva-rūpāḥ paśavo vadanti | sā no mandreṣam-ūrjaṃ duhānā dhenur-vāg-asmān-upa suṣṭutaitu || 10 ||
entries.translation: The deities (deva) brought forth (ajanayanta) the Goddess (devī) of Speech (vāc), and every (viśva) form (rūpa) of creature (paśu) communicates (vadanti) through her (tāṃ). May she (sā)—the melodious (mandrā) cow (dhenu) of speech (vāc), milking (duhānā) for us (naḥ) sustenance (iṣ) and vitality (ūrj)—come (etu) close (upa) to us (asmān), being well-praised (su-stutā).

entries.title: Bowing to Diverse Forms of Devī
entries.transliteration: kālarātrīṃ brahma-stutāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ skanda-mātaram | sarasvatīm-aditiṃ dakṣa-duhitaraṃ namāmaḥ pāvanāṃ śivām || 11 ||
entries.translation: To Kālarātrī, who is praised (stutā) by Brahmā, Vaiṣṇavī, the mother (mātṛ) of Skanda, Sarasvatī, and Aditi [mother of the Ādityas], the daughter (duhitṛ) of Dakṣa, we bow down (namāmaḥ) to she who purifies (pāvanā), she who is auspicious (śivā).

entries.title: Mahālakṣmī Gāyatrī
entries.transliteration: mahālakṣmyai ca vidmahe sarva-śaktyai ca dhīmahi | tanno devī pracodayāt || 12 ||
entries.translation: We contemplate (vidmahe) and (ca) set our minds (dhīmahi) upon Mahālakṣmī, who embodies all (sarva) the powers (śakti). May that (tat) Goddess (devī) guide us (naḥ) forward (pracodayāt).

entries.title: Hymn to Devī as Aditi
entries.transliteration: aditirhyajaniṣṭa dakṣa yā duhitā tava | tāṃ devā anvajāyanta bhadrā amṛtabandhavaḥ || 13 ||
entries.translation: Aditi indeed (hi) was born (ajaniṣṭa) as your (tava) daughter (duhitṛ), O Dakṣa! And from (anu-) her (tāṃ), those auspicious (bhadra) deities (deva), in the lineage (bandhu) of immortality (amṛta), [i.e., the Ādityas] were born (-ajāyanta).

entries.title: Mantroddhāra of the Pañcadaśākṣarī
entries.transliteration: kāmo yoniḥ kamalā vajra-pāṇir- guhā hasā mātariśvābhram-indraḥ | punar-guhā sakalā māyayā ca purūcyaiṣā viśva-mātādi-vidyom || 14 ||
entries.translation: [The phoneme of] desire (kāma) [ka], [the phoneme shaped like a] womb (yoni) [e], [the phonemes of the] lotus (kamalā) [i.e., Lakṣmī] [ī], [the] bearer-of-the-thunderbolt (Vajrapāṇi) [i.e., Indra, whose phoneme is] [la], [the] hidden one (guhā) [hrīṃ]; [the phonemes] ha and sa (hasā), [of the] wind deity (Mātariśvan) [ka], cloud (abhra) [ha], lord of deities (Indra) [la], and again (punar) the hidden one (guhā) [hrīṃ]; [the phonemes] sa-ka-la (sakalā), and (ca) together with [the] magical power (māyā) [phoneme] [hrīṃ]: this (eṣā) [mantra of ka-e-ī-la-hrīṃ, ha-sa-ka-ha-la-hrīṃ, sa-ka-la-hrīṃ] is to be abundantly (puru) recited (ucyā) as the primordial (ādi) knowledge (vidyā), the mother (mātṛ) of the universe (viśva). Oṃ.

entries.title: Visualization of Mahā Tripurasundarī
entries.transliteration: eṣātmaśaktiḥ | eṣā viśvamohinī | pāśāṅkuśa-dhanur-bāṇa-dharā | eṣā śrī-mahā-vidyā | ya evaṃ veda sa śokaṃ tarati || 15 ||
entries.translation: She (eṣā) is the power (śakti) of the self (ātman). She (eṣā) is the one who enchants (mohinī) the universe (viśva). Bearing (dharā) the noose (pāśa), goad (aṅkuśa), bow (dhanus), and arrows (bāṇa). She (eṣā) is the great-wisdom-goddess (śrīmahāvidyā). Whoever (yaḥ) knows (veda ) thus (evam) will cross over (tarati) all sorrow (śoka).

entries.title: Requesting Protection from Bhagavatī
entries.transliteration: namaste astu bhagavati mātar-asmān-pāhi sarvataḥ || 16 ||
entries.translation: Let there be (astu) reverence (namas) to you (te), O Goddess (bhagavatī). Mother (mātṛ), protect (pāhi) us (asmān) in every direction (sarvatas).

entries.title: Enumerating the Forms of Devī
entries.transliteration: saiṣāṣṭau vasavaḥ | saiṣaikādaśa rudrāḥ | saiṣā dvādaśādityāḥ | saiṣā viśvedevāḥ somapā asomapāś ca | She (sā) herself (eṣā) [is] the eight (aṣṭa) Vasus. She (sā) herself (eṣā) [is] the eleven (ekādaśa) Rudras. She (sā) herself (eṣā) [is] the twelve (dvādaśa) Ādityas. She (sā) herself (eṣā) [is] the Viśvedevas: [both] those who drink soma (somapā) and (ca) those who drink what is not soma (asomapā). She (sā) herself (eṣā) [is] the malevolent spirits (yātudhāna), the asuras, the demons (rakṣas), the flesh-eating spirits (piśāca), the demigods (yakṣa), and the perfected masters (siddha). She (sā) herself (eṣā) [is] the [three guṇas or qualities of prakṛti] of light-clarity (sattva), heat-passion (rajas), and darkness-dullness (tamas). saiṣā yātudhānā asurā rakṣāṃsi piśācā yakṣāḥ siddhāḥ | saiṣā sattvarajastamāṃsi | saiṣā brahmaviṣṇurudrarūpiṇī | saiṣā prajāpatīndramanavaḥ | saiṣā grahanakṣatrajyotīṃṣi | kalākāṣṭhādikālarūpiṇī | tām ahaṃ praṇaumi nityam | pāpāpahāriṇīṃ devīṃ bhukti-mukti-pradāyinīm | anantāṃ vijayāṃ śuddhāṃ śaraṇyāṃ śivadāṃ śivām || 17 ||
entries.translation: She (sā) herself (eṣā) [is] the deities of creation (Brahmā), sustenance (Viṣṇu), and destruction (Rudra). She (sā) herself (eṣā) [is] Prajāpati [the creator deity], Indra [the chief of deities], and the Manus [the progenitors of mankind]. She (sā) herself (eṣā) [is] the planets (graha), the star- constellations (nakṣatra), and the celestial bodies (jyotis). She is of the form of (rūpiṇī) time (kāla): [measured in] the digits of the moon [that mark the passage of time] (kalā), the [further] subdivisions of time (kāṣṭhā), and so on (ādi). Her (tām), I (aham) always (nityam) revere (praṇaumi): The Goddess (devī) who is the remover (apahāriṇī) of sins (pāpa) and the bestower (pradāyinī) of worldly enjoyment (bhukti) and spiritual liberation (mukti). Who is without end (anantā), victorious (vijayā), pure (śuddhā), a refuge (śaraṇyā), the giver of peace (śivadā), the auspicious one (śivā).

entries.title: Mantroddhāra of the Devī Praṇava
entries.transliteration: viyad-īkāra-saṃyuktaṃ vīti-hotra-samanvitam | ardhendu-lasitaṃ devyā bījaṃ sarvārtha-sādhakam || 18 ||
entries.translation: [The phoneme of] space (viyat)  [ha] combined with (saṃyukta) the phoneme ī (īkāra), accompanied by (samanvita) [the phoneme of the sacrificial] fire (vītihotra) [i.e., Agni whose phoneme is] [ra], and adorned (lasita) with the half-moon (ardhendu) [ṃ] [makes hrīṃ]: the seed (bīja) [mantra] of the Goddess (devī), which accomplishes (sādhaka) all (sarva) of life’s aims (artha).

entries.title: Phalaśruti of Devī Praṇava Mantra
entries.transliteration: evam-ekākṣaraṃ brahma yatayaḥ śuddha-cetasaḥ | dhyāyanti paramānanda-mayā jñānāmburāśayaḥ || 19 ||
entries.translation: Those self-restrained ones (yati) who meditate (dhyāyanti) in this way (evam) upon this one-syllable (ekākṣara) Brahman [i.e., hrīṃ] with pure (śuddha) thoughts (cetas) are filled with (-maya) the highest (parama) bliss (ānanda), [and become] oceans (amburāśi) of wisdom (jñāna).

entries.title: Mantroddhāra of Navārṇa
entries.transliteration: vāṅ-māyā brahmasūs-tasmāt ṣaṣṭhaṃ vaktra-samanvitam | sūryo ’vāma-śrotra-bindu-saṃyuktaṣ-ṭāttṛtīyakaḥ | nārāyaṇena sammiśro vāyuś-cādharayuk-tataḥ | vicce navārṇako ’rṇaḥ syān-mahad-ānanda-dāyakaḥ || 20 ||
entries.translation: The [bīja mantra of] speech (vāc) [of Vāgdevī is aiṃ], the [bīja mantra of] magical power (māyā) [is hrīṃ], the creator deity’s son (brahmasū) [is Kāmadeva, the deity of desire, and the bīja mantra of kāma is klīṃ], the sixth (ṣaṣṭha) [letter counting from] that [ka of klīṃ] (tasmāt) [is ca; and ca] endowed with (samanvita) the [nyāsa phoneme of the] mouth (vaktra) [ā, makes cā], [the phoneme of the] sun (sūrya) [ma], [the nyāsa phoneme of the] right (avāma) ear (śrotra) [u] joined together (saṃyukta) with the point (bindu) [ṃ], the third (tṛtīyaka) [phoneme] counting from ṭa [is ḍa] combined (sammiśra) with [the bīja mantra of] Nārāyaṇa [ā, makes ḍā], the [phoneme] of the wind deity (Vāyu) [ya] joined (yuk) with the [nyāsa phoneme of the] lower (adhara) [lip] [ai, makes yai], afterward (tataḥ) is “vicce”: this forms (syāt) the nine-lettered (nava-arṇaka) mantra (arṇa) [aiṃ-hrīṃ-klīṃ-cā-muṇ-ḍā-yai- vic-ce], the giver (dāyaka) of great bliss (mahadānanda).

entries.title: Visualization of Bhuvaneśvarī
entries.transliteration: hṛtpuṇḍarīka-madhyasthāṃ prātaḥsūrya-samaprabhām | pāśāṅkuśa-dharāṃ saumyāṃ varadābhaya-hastakām | trinetrāṃ rakta-vasanāṃ bhakta-kāma-dughāṃ bhaje || 21 ||
entries.translation: She who is situated in the center (madhyasthā) of the lotus of the heart (hṛtpuṇḍarīka), with the same luster (samaprabhā) as the morning (prātar) sun (sūrya), bearing (dharā) the noose (pāśa) and goad (aṅkuśa), peaceful (saumyā), displaying the hand gestures (hastaka) of granting blessings (varada) and dispelling fear (abhaya), three-eyed (trinetrā), wearing blood- red (rakta) [colored] garments (vasana), who grants (dughā) the desires (kāma) of her devotees (bhakta)—her, I worship (bhaje).

entries.title: Reverence to Mahādevī
entries.transliteration: namāmi tvāṃ mahādevīṃ mahābhaya-vināśinīm | mahā-durga-praśamanīṃ mahā-kāruṇya-rūpiṇīm || 22 ||
entries.translation: I revere (namāmi) you (tvāṃ), O Great Goddess (mahādevī), the destroyer (vināśinī) of great fear (mahābhaya), who pacifies (praśamanī) great (mahā) difficulties (durga) [and] is the embodiment (rūpiṇī) of great (mahā) compassion (kāruṇya).

entries.title: Transcendent Names of Devī
entries.transliteration: yasyāḥ svarūpaṃ brahmādayo na jānanti tasmād ucyate ajñeyā | yasyā anto na labhyate tasmād ucyate anantā | yasyā lakṣyaṃ nopalakṣyate tasmād ucyate alakṣyā | yasyā jananaṃ nopalabhyate tasmād ucyate ajā | ekaiva sarvatra vartate tasmād ucyate ekā | ekaiva viśvarūpiṇī tasmād ucyate naikā | ata evocyate ajñeyānantālakṣyājaikā naiketi || 23 ||
entries.translation: Whose (yasyāḥ) true form (svarūpa) even Brahmā and other deities (brahmādi) do not (na) know (jānanti)—she is therefore (tasmād) called (ucyate) “the unknowable” (ajñeyā). Whose (yasyā) end (anta) cannot (na) be found (labhyate)—she is therefore (tasmād) called (ucyate) “the endless” (anantā). Whose (yasyā) distinctive signs (lakṣya) cannot (na) be signified (upalakṣyate)—she is therefore (tasmād) called (ucyate) “the signless” (alakṣyā). Whose (yasyā) birth (janana) cannot (na) be found (upalabhyate)—she is therefore (tasmād) called (ucyate) “the unborn” (ajā). She alone (ekā eva) exists (vartate) everywhere (sarvatra)— she is therefore (tasmād) called (ucyate) “singular” (ekā). She alone (ekā eva) is of the form of the [multifarious] universe (viśvarūpiṇī)—she is therefore (tasmād) called (ucyate) “not- singular” (na-ekā). Indeed (eva), it is for this reason (atas), she is called (ucyate) thus (iti): “the unknowable-endless-signless-unborn-singular- [and]-not-singular” (ajñeyā-anantā-alakṣyā-ajā-ekā-na-ekā).

entries.title: Essential Forms of Devī
entries.transliteration: mantrāṇāṃ mātṛkā devī śabdānāṃ jñāna-rūpiṇī | jñānānāṃ cinmayātītā śūnyānāṃ śūnya-sākṣiṇī | yasyāḥ parataraṃ nāsti saiṣā durgā prakīrtitā || 24 ||
entries.translation: Among mantras, the Goddess (devī) is the phonemes (mātṛkā) [from which mantras are essentially made]. Among words (śabda), she is of the nature (rūpiṇī) of cognition (jñāna) [which senses the essence of words, their meaning]. Among modes of cognition (jñāna), she is that transcendent consciousness (cinmayātītā) [that pervades and grasps all cognitive modes]. Among the void states (śūnya), she is the consciousness who is witness (sākṣiṇī) of those void states (śūnya). Beyond whom (yasyāḥ) there is none (nāsti) superior (paratara): this very goddess (eṣā), she (sā) is proclaimed (prakīrtitā) as Durgā.

entries.title: Reverence to Durgā
entries.transliteration: tāṃ durgāṃ durgamāṃ devīṃ durācāra-vighātinīm | namāmi bhavabhīto ’haṃ saṃsārārṇava-tāriṇīm || 25 ||
entries.translation: To Durgā—the unattainable (durgamā) goddess (devī) who removes (vighātinī) all wrong conduct (durācāra)—being fearful (bhīta) of what I may become (bhava), I offer her (tāṃ) my reverence (namāmi): she is the transporter across (tāriṇī) the ocean (arṇava) of cyclic conditioned becoming (saṃsāra).

entries.title: Phalaśruti of Devī Atharvaśīrṣa I
entries.transliteration: idam-atharvaśīrṣaṃ yo ’dhīte sa pañcātharvaśīrṣa-japa-phalam-āpnoti | idam-atharvaśīrṣam ajñātvā yo ’rcāṃ sthāpayati | śatalakṣaṃ prajaptvā ’pi so ’rcāsiddhiṃ na vindati | śatam aṣṭottaraṃ cāsya puraścaryā-vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ | daśavāraṃ paṭhed yas tu sadyaḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate | mahā-durgāṇi tarati mahādevyāḥ prasādataḥ || 26 ||
entries.translation: One (yaḥ) who studies (adhīte) this (idam) [Devī] Atharvaśīrṣa receives (āpnoti) the [same] fruits (phala) as the recitation (japa) of five (pañca) Atharvaśīrṣas. One (yaḥ) who establishes (sthāpayati) an image to worship (arcā) without knowing (ajñātvā) this (idam) Atharvaśīrṣa— even (api) after reciting (prajaptvā) [a mantra] a hundred (śata) lakh (lakṣa) [i.e., 10 million] times—will not (na) attain (vindati) success (siddhi) in that worship (arcā). One hundred (śata) plus (uttara) eight (aṣṭa) [i.e., 108] [recitations] of this (asya) [Atharvaśīrṣa] is recalled (smṛta) to be the procedure (vidhi) for preliminary initiatory rites (puraścaryā). One (yaḥ) who would recite (paṭhet) [this Atharvaśīrṣa] ten (daśa) times (vāra), indeed (tu), immediately (sadyas) will be released (pramucyate) from one’s wrongdoings (pāpa). [One] crosses over (tarati) immense (mahā-) difficulties (durga) by the blessings (prasāda) of the Great Goddess (mahādevī).

entries.title: Phalaśruti of Devī Atharvaśīrṣa II
entries.transliteration: sāyam adhīyāno divasakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ nāśayati | prātar adhīyāno rātrikṛtaṃ pāpaṃ nāśayati | sāyaṃ prātaḥ prayuñjāno apāpo bhavati | niśīthe turīyasandhyāyāṃ japtvā vāksiddhir bhavati | nūtanāyāṃ pratimāyāṃ japtvā devatāsānnidhyaṃ bhavati | prāṇapratiṣṭhāyāṃ japtvā Reciting (adhīyāna) [this Atharvaśīrṣa] in the evening (sāyam) destroys (nāśayati) all wrongdoings (pāpa) committed (kṛta) during the day (divasa). Reciting (adhīyāna) [this Atharvaśīrṣa] in the morning (prātar) destroys (nāśayati) all wrongdoings (pāpa) committed (kṛta) during the night (rātri). Combining recitation (prayuñjāna) [of this Atharvaśīrṣa] in the evening (sāyam) and in the morning (prātar), one [therefore] becomes (bhavati) [completely] free of wrongdoing (apāpa). Having recited (japtvā) [this Atharvaśīrṣa] at midnight (niśītha)—at the fourth (turīya) junction of the day (sandhyā) [alongside dawn, noon, and dusk]—the perfection (siddhi) of speech (vāc) occurs (bhavati). Having recited (japtvā) [this Atharvaśīrṣa] before a new (nūtana) image (pratimā), the presence (sānnidhya) of the deity (devatā) [within the image] occurs (bhavati). Having recited (japtvā) [this Atharvaśīrṣa] at the installation (pratiṣṭhā) of life (prāṇa) [into the image], the installation prāṇānāṃ pratiṣṭhā bhavati | bhaumāśvinyāṃ mahādevīsannidhau japtvā mahāmṛtyuṃ tarati | sa mahāmṛtyuṃ tarati | ya evaṃ veda | ityupaniṣat || 27 ||
entries.translation: (pratiṣṭhā) of life (prāṇa) occurs (bhavati). Having recited (japtvā) [this Atharvaśīrṣa] in the presence (sannidhi) of the Great Goddess (mahādevī) on [amṛtasiddhiyoga, the astrological combination of] the day of Mars (bhauma) [i.e., Tuesday] and the Aśvinī [lunar mansion], great death (mahāmṛtyu) is crossed over (tarati). One (saḥ) crosses over (tarati) great death (mahāmṛtyu), the one who (yaḥ) knows (veda) thus (evam). Thus ends (iti) the esoteric teaching (upaniṣad).
